findings.title: Variable subtraction can be mistaken for a prose aside
findings.problem: MATH_SIGN recognizes ASCII subtraction only between two digits or with spaces around the minus sign. MATH_BEFORE also does not recognize a preceding identifier as an implicit multiplication factor. Consequently, speakable("VO2 = CO (CaO2-CvO2).") produces "VO2 equals CO, CaO2-CvO2." The parentheses establishing the product have become a comma-separated list, contradicting the guarantee that arithmetic grouping is preserved.
findings.failure_scenario: A cardiac oxygen-consumption rationale uses the Fick relationship written as `VO2 = CO (CaO2-CvO2).` The script builder removes its meaningful grouping. The audio gate then checks the recording against that already-altered script, so it cannot detect the corruption before students hear it.
findings.fix: Conservatively preserve parentheses containing symbolic subtraction, including unspaced ASCII minus, and parentheses adjacent to identifiers that may be multiplication factors. Add an exact-output regression for this formula; uncertain mathematical groups should remain unchanged or be refused for voicing.

assessment: One unsafe bracket rewrite can alter a clinical formula before the audio accuracy gate sees it. The added arithmetic tests miss this case.
